The shell reaches a closed state of stability
The properties of the first period are recorded in the periodic law
The sequence links to the second period starting with Lithium
The p-orbital introduces further branching in the valence shell
Electrons occupy degenerate orbitals simultaneously before pairing
Carbon achieves a stable tetrahedral bonding potential
Highly reactive Fluorine seeks electron gain to resolve instability
Neon completes the second shell closure
The second period properties are fixed in the table
The sequence continues through the transition metals
The d-block introduces complex sub-shell branching
Alpha emission reduces the atomic number of heavy unstable nuclei
Technetium fails to find a stable isotopic configuration
Lead reaches the end of the stable nuclear sequence
The Oganesson boundary marks the current limit of the periodic system
